criteria.criterion: The extension is installable as a governed VSIX and exposes VI History on eligible VIs in trusted Git workspaces.
criteria.nextAction: Sustain the installed command surface while release packaging is hardened.

criteria.criterion: Reliable NI comparison-report execution remains proven on the governed runtime path.
criteria.nextAction: Sustain the live runtime proof while releaseability is added.

criteria.criterion: The dashboard is the default expert review surface for one VI across at least three commits.
criteria.nextAction: Sustain the dashboard while release blockers are removed.

criteria.criterion: Long-running report and dashboard flows expose bounded progress, cancellation, trust-aware refusals, and runtime-doctor guidance without requiring raw-log inspection first.
criteria.blocker: The extension-facing developer experience is still partial and not yet governed as a full release-ready UX layer.
criteria.nextAction: Finish the remaining progress/trust UX surfaces under ISSUE-0403.

criteria.criterion: A reviewer can create a separate decision record from retained dashboard evidence through a governed product flow.
criteria.blocker: The canonical scenario flow exists, but extension-facing decision-record creation is not yet implemented.
criteria.nextAction: Extend the retained scenario flow into the extension UX after the ship-control tranche stabilizes.

criteria.criterion: A SemVer tag produces a versioned VSIX artifact and retained release evidence that point to the exact installable extension version.
criteria.blocker: The GitLab release lane is configured to package a versioned VSIX and release manifest, but the first successful SemVer-tagged release run has not yet been retained as ship evidence.
criteria.nextAction: Run the first governed SemVer tag pipeline and retain the generated VSIX plus release manifest as release evidence.
